overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation on the complaint: the Committee's minutes were sufficiently detailed, the bias and single-candidate claims were declined (the latter as untimely), though the AG expressed concern about a Board chair's email to the full Board.

allegations.summary: Complainant said Committee minutes of the Nov. 20 and 21 meetings did not publish the uniform interview questions asked or the candidates' answers.
allegations.key_passage: Minutes of the Committee’s November 21 meeting summarize the interviews and therefore conform to the requirements of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant said Nov. 21 minutes omitted details of about 15-20 positive reference letters and two negative letters about a candidate.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Committee did not discuss the letters, it did not violate the Open Meeting Law by omitting details about the letters in the minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant said Nov. 21 minutes did not reference a letter the complainant sent to the Committee chair.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Committee did not discuss the letters, it did not violate the Open Meeting Law by omitting details about the letters in the minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant said the Nov. 21 minutes did not record a vote to recommend a candidate for the position.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee, however, reached a consensus to recommend Mr. Wolf without holding a vote.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee's minutes reflected bias toward one candidate and that another was wrongly eliminated over his start date.
allegations.key_passage: because we do not review a public body’s actions for bias, we decline to review the allegation that the Committee did not recommend Matt Smith as a bona fide candidate

allegations.summary: Alleged the Committee violated the law by recommending only one candidate for Highway Superintendent after withdrawals.
allegations.key_passage: As the complaint was filed on May 5, 2025, it was not timely as to this allegation.

allegations.summary: Alleged the Board violated the law by voting to offer the position to the sole remaining candidate.
allegations.key_passage: Any failure to conform with the Open Meeting Law was reasonably discoverable on November 26, 2024.

allegations.summary: Not alleged by complainant: AG voiced concern that the Board chair emailed the full Board about a candidate's withdrawal instead of at a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Such communication should have occurred in a properly posted meeting, not via email.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
